1. [test/orders.js](C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:18): `averageItemPrice` is semantically misleading. It divides total revenue by `items.length`, so orders with `qty > 1` return an average per line item, not per unit. I would either rename it to match behavior or compute `sum(price * qty) / sum(qty)`.

2. [test/orders.js](C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:19): `averageItemPrice` does not handle an empty array. `0 / 0` yields `NaN`. I would return `0` or throw a clear error, depending on expected API behavior.

3. [test/orders.js](C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:6): `calcTotal` assumes every entry has numeric `price` and `qty`. A missing field or string value can throw or produce `NaN`. I would validate inputs or coerce defensively if this module can receive untrusted data.

4. [test/orders.js](C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:24): `formatOrder` assumes `order`, `order.items`, and each item shape are present. A malformed order object will throw while formatting. I would add basic guards if this is used at a boundary.

5. [test/orders.js](C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:13): discount handling is permissive but underspecified. Unknown codes silently do nothing, which may be fine, but I would make that explicit in tests and consider normalizing case if user-entered codes are expected.

Main hardening priority after the crash is `averageItemPrice`, because it has both a correctness bug and a bad empty-input case.
